what: 4. A boundary-element leadfield, and validating it
title: EEG forward models: from a source space to a validated leadfield
text: bemLeadfield() solves problem numerically double-layer collocation BEM, use realistic (non-spherical) head. sphere mesh can score analytic answer leadfieldRDM(): relative difference measure (RDM) captures topography error (0 = identical), magnitude ratio (MAG) captures amplitude. topography (RDM) already close improves mesh refined, amplitude (MAG) carries well-known coarse-collocation bias: source localization invariant global leadfield scale, RDM metric trust validation; absolute amplitude bias affect inverse solution.
code: few_sources <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0.5), c(0.3, 0, 0.2), c(0, 0.35, 0.1))  bem <- bemLeadfield(mesh, conductivities = c(0.33, 0), electrodes, few_sources) ana <- sphereLeadfield(electrodes, few_sources)  leadfieldRDM(bem, ana) #>       RDM       MAG  #> 0.2172864 0.4273529 rdm_at <- function(sub) {   m <- icosphere(sub)   e <- m$vertices   leadfieldRDM(bemLeadfield(m, c(0.33, 0), e, few_sources),                sphereLeadfield(e, few_sources)) } rbind(`icosphere(1)` = rdm_at(1),       `icosphere(2)` = rdm_at(2)) #>                    RDM       MAG #> icosphere(1) 0.4335262 0.4546159 #> icosphere(2) 0.2178245 0.4244965

what: Boundary element method (BEM) EEG leadfield — bemLeadfield
title: Boundary element method (BEM) EEG leadfield — bemLeadfield
text: Solves piecewise-homogeneous EEG forward problem classic collocation double-layer boundary element method (Geselowitz boundary integral, van Oosterom-Strackee solid angles, average-reference deflation) one nested triangulated surfaces. Validated analytic single-sphere solution: sphere mesh leadfield topography matches small relative difference measure (RDM); absolute amplitude carries usual coarse-collocation bias, use RDM (topography) validation note source localization invariant global leadfield scale.
